the results obtained from these experiments have not only provided the basis of the design and construction of the sensitive rain recording instruments, but also have given the first quantitative data of small-scale variations in rainfall rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the raindrop spectra are well described by a power law, and that the power law index is a function of the rain rate.

we have developed and tested a new type of rainfall recorder, the "raindrop size spectrometer," which has been used to measure raindrop size distributions and to study the small scale variations of rainfall intensity.
we have developed an instrument capable of recording rainfall rate variations with an accuracy of 0.01mm/hr, a time resolution of 0.1 sec and a dynamic range of 1000 : 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rain rate can be estimated from the attenuation of a single frequency, but that the accuracy of this estimate can be improved by using a second frequency.
the small-scale variations in rainfall rate are important for the design of millimeter-wave radar systems.
the rain-rate variability is not only a function of the rain rate but is also a function of the time scale of interest.
